reason: Executive Order 6526 of December 21, 1933 states: "do order that the application for exemption by the Southern Plow Manufacturers Association, be and is hereby denied". A denial of an application for exemption from a code commands nothing after it issues: its command was performed and exhausted on December 21, 1933, the date the order was signed, and the order states no later effective date. The applicant's continuing obligation after the denial is the code's own operation, which the order approving the Farm Equipment Code governs and which ended with the repeal; it is not a surviving command of the denial. The Administrator's report of November 21, 1933 that the order adopts is a recital, not a deadline or a command. The later event is the repeal on June 14, 1935: section 2 of S.J. Res. 113 provides "All the provisions of Title I of such Act delegating power to the President to approve or prescribe codes of fair competition and providing for the enforcement of such codes are hereby repealed". Schechter (295 U.S. 495, decided May 27, 1935) is recorded as a validity characterization, not an end date.
